chunks: Yaqub narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The people of Mecca, when they visit the House and enter their homes, then return to Mina, complete the prayer; and if they do not enter their homes, they shorten it.
ai.seo_question: When should the residents of Mecca shorten their prayers during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal status of Mecca’s residents (Ahl al-Makkah) as permanent residents rather than travelers, contingent upon their actual movement. It establishes that entering one's home resets the traveler's status, thereby requiring full prayers, whereas remaining in transit preserves the right to shorten them. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on physical presence and intent in determining the applicability of travel concessions during Hajj rituals.
